subject: Civil Engineering
title: Fire Resistance of Concrete
description: A short lesson to help you apply Fire Resistance of Concrete.

hook.text: Steel buildings collapse in fire. Concrete buildings survive — most of the time.

buildup.text: Concrete doesn't burn. It insulates the steel rebar inside from extreme heat.

discovery.text: At 600°C, concrete loses about 50% of its strength. At 1,000°C, it crumbles.

twist.text: High-strength concrete spalls explosively in fire — steam pressure blows off the surface.

climax.text: Polypropylene fibers melt in fire, creating escape channels for steam — preventing spalling.

punchline.text: Concrete resists fire better than any other building material — but it has limits.

quiz.question: Why does high-strength concrete spall explosively in fire?
options: The aggregate expands faster than the cement paste
Dense concrete traps steam pressure that builds up and blasts off the surface
High-strength concrete contains flammable chemical admixtures

details.summary: Concrete provides excellent fire resistance because it does not burn, has low thermal conductivity that slows heat penetration, and maintains significant strength up to about 300 degrees Celsius. However, explosive spalling can occur when moisture trapped inside vaporizes rapidly under extreme heat.
details.whyItMatters: Concrete's fire resistance is a major advantage over steel structures, which lose strength rapidly above 500 degrees. Fire rating requirements for concrete structures protect occupants during evacuation and enable structural survival.
takeaways: Concrete does not burn and conducts heat slowly, protecting reinforcement
Explosive spalling occurs when trapped moisture vaporizes under extreme heat
Polypropylene fibers melt to create escape channels for steam pressure

faq.question: Why does high-strength concrete spall more severely in fires?
faq.answer: High-strength concrete has very low permeability that traps moisture with no escape path. As fire heats the surface, trapped water vaporizes and builds steam pressure. Eventually the pressure exceeds concrete tensile strength, causing violent explosive spalling that exposes reinforcement.

faq.question: How do polypropylene fibers improve fire resistance of concrete?
faq.answer: Polypropylene fibers melt at about 160 degrees Celsius, well below fire temperatures. The melted fibers create a network of fine channels through the concrete that allow steam to escape, preventing the pressure buildup that causes explosive spalling.
